title: Group scope-guard lines only by retry link, not cited job ids
summary: In scope_guard.rs, stop joining a request to a line because its text mentions another job's id; group only by the retry link (and the existing same-text re-ask). A request citing a paused line's jobs as evidence starts its own line and is not paused. Audience: the operator whose unrelated fix was refused.

defaults_applied.how: New tests plus cargo test, clippy -D warnings and fmt criteria.
Remove the id-in-text grouping rule rather than special-casing the one refused request.
Tests exercise grouping and the pause outcome for evidence-citing vs retry requests.
One focused change in scope_guard.rs and the changelog.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: 'Explicit follow-up of a named job' is the existing retry link ('try again on <job>'); no new follow-up syntax is added.
The same-text re-ask link stays, as the request only removes id-in-text grouping.
The quotes field may be removed or left unused; either is fine if clippy is clean.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new unit test in scope_guard.rs shows a request whose text cites jobs of a paused line is in its own line (group_lines) and is not refused as paused; run `cargo test -p athena-core scope_guard`.
A test shows a retry (retry_of link) of the paused line is still grouped into it and refused; run `cargo test -p athena-core scope_guard`, and the existing retry_refuses_paused_line passes.

group_lines and request_records in scope_guard.rs no longer link a request to another by job ids found in its text (diff shows the quotes link removed from grouping); doc comments describe grouping by retry link and same-text re-ask only.
Tests that relied on quote grouping (grouping_joins_retries_and_quoting_requests and any others) are updated to the new rule; `cargo test` passes for the whole workspace.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing that citing job ids as evidence no longer groups a request into that line (git diff shows it).

hard_reason: Changes the scope guard's rule for grouping requests into lines, which decides whether work is refused or paused.
